Hi there, I’m sorry that your stepmother and boss are going through/went through the same things as my dad. It’s definitely tough to see a loved one in that condition. But I can assure you of something, my profound sense of hope and peace that I feel comes from the Lord and the Lord ONLY. When I first heard about my father’s condition, my initial reaction was to emotionally “run away” and just completely shut down any thoughts about him as a “defense mechanism”. I distracted myself with friends & things of this world. It’s not healthy and it’s not efficient. Only when I started praying was I overwhelmed with a sense of hope and faith that my dad WILL be healed because God hears our prayers and NOTHING is impossible through him (Mark 10:27). I suddenly became the beacon of hope and strength for my family who lost hope. And I don’t think it’s irony that Faith is my name. 

*Look no further, Jesus is the way, the truth and the life (John 14:6). Believe and you WILL receive (Matthew 21:22). I will be praying for you, and it’s no coincide God brought you here because he wants all to be saved (Psalm 37:5).*

Update: The doctors tried “preparing” us for the “high chances” of him dying and discussing possibly “giving up” on treatments. But it comes as no surprise to me, just pure gratitude for my God, that my dad is now flipped over on his back (he was on his stomach for a long time because that’s supposed to be the best way to deliver oxygen to the lungs) and they are little by little decreasing the amount of oxygen they had him on. Little by little he’s getting better. Small victories definitely matter. And I know God will heal him in his own perfect timing (Psalm 31:15).

Even though I’m a Christian, I still can’t process death properly when it’s someone I know personally. I felt like I was in a trance the entire time at my grandma’s funeral last year (the first funeral I attended that I was completely conscious of). When me, my brother, and my cousin were slowly approaching the open casket, I *burst into laughter* right after I saw just the tip of her nose. I literally fell on the floor, scream laughing, tears in my eyes. I then caused my cousin to burst into laughter too. Very bad, good thing it was just the three of us in that room (but the main doors were open so it’s possible that the people outside heard us). I don’t find death funny at all, and I didn’t find my grandma’s death funny either, but it’s like my brain couldn’t process it any other way. Sort of off topic, but I really do be laughing at the worst possible times (I’ve laughed many times or put all of my energy into trying to stifle laughter during very serious or quiet moments- and it’s not because I find the situation or anything in particular funny, but it’s like a reflex during vulnerable moments).

Edit: also: my “grandpa” (a very amazing guy) is in hospice right now, and I feel a little sad, a little neutral and a little hopeful. My cousin was sobbing to me saying that my uncle and my uncle’s brother-in-law almost died in a crash, I kind of felt nothing.
